summary: This memo gives an overview of version 2 of the Internet-standard Network Management Framework, called SNMPv2. This early version of SNMPv2 is historic.

eli5.summary: SNMP is how network managers ask devices about their health. This paper introduces the second version of that system. It is historic.

subtitle: Overview of the Internet-standard framework for network management, version 2.

tldr.problem: Networks need a standard way for monitoring stations to query and control devices like routers and servers to understand the health and status of network infrastructure.
tldr.mechanism: SNMPv2 extends the original SNMP framework with improved structure definitions, textual conventions, protocol operations, transport mappings, management information bases, administrative security models, and conformance statements to make network management more consistent and secure.
tldr.outcome: This early version of SNMPv2 is now Historic, having been refined in later specifications. The framework established the architecture used by modern network management systems.

today: RFC 1441 is Historic. This early introduction to SNMPv2 was part of an initial SNMPv2 specification that evolved and was refined. Modern network management uses SNMPv3 and other frameworks, but the architecture and concepts introduced here remain foundational to network management systems.

sections.title: SNMP and Network Management
sections.content: SNMP (Simple Network Management Protocol) is the standard for Internet network management. This RFC introduces version 2 of the framework, derived from the original SNMPv1, which consisted of three documents: RFC 1155 defining the Structure of Management Information (SMI) for describing managed objects, RFC 1212 providing concise descriptions for SMI, and RFC 1157 defining the protocol itself. SNMPv2 builds on this foundation with improvements across multiple areas. A network management system contains managed devices (hosts, routers, servers) each with an agent providing access to management information, at least one management station running management applications, and a protocol conveying management information between agents and stations. Operations occur under an administrative framework defining authentication and authorization policies.
sections.eli5: Network managers need to ask devices about their status. SNMP is how they do it. Version 2 is an improved design for that conversation.

sections.title: Information Structure and Objects
sections.content: SNMPv2 organizes management information as a collection of managed objects in a virtual information store called the Management Information Base (MIB). Related objects are grouped in MIB modules written using ASN.1 (Abstract Syntax Notation One), a standard for specifying data structures. The SMI is divided into three parts. Module definitions describe information modules using the MODULE-IDENTITY macro to express module semantics. Object definitions describe managed objects using the OBJECT-TYPE macro to specify syntax and semantics. Notification definitions describe unsolicited transmissions of management information using the NOTIFICATION-TYPE macro. Additionally, textual conventions allow MIB designers to define new types with names similar to base SMI types but with more precise semantics, expressed using the TEXTUAL-CONVENTION macro.
sections.eli5: Management information is organized like a filing cabinet with labeled drawers. Each drawer holds facts about the device, described in a standard way so everyone understands what they mean.

sections.title: Message Exchange and Transport
sections.content: The management protocol exchanges messages conveying management information between agents and management stations. Each message is a wrapper encapsulating a Protocol Data Unit (PDU) whose form and meaning are determined by an administrative framework defining authentication and authorization policies. SNMPv2 may be used over a variety of protocol suites. The preferred mapping is onto UDP (User Datagram Protocol), and systems choosing other mappings should provide proxy service to the UDP mapping for greatest interoperability. The management protocol defines the operations for sending and receiving PDUs with respect to message format, authentication, and authorization.
sections.eli5: The manager sends a message to an agent asking for information. The message has a secure wrapper that says who is asking and what they are allowed to do. The agent checks the wrapper and sends back the answer.

sections.title: Administration and Security
sections.content: SNMPv2 parties are conceptual virtual execution contexts whose operations are restricted to an administratively defined subset of operations. Each party has a single authentication protocol and a single privacy protocol. The Administrative Model defines party behavior, restricting what operations that party can perform and what information it can access. Security Protocols define the authentication and privacy protocols used by parties. The Party MIB defines managed objects describing properties of SNMPv2 parties. This administrative framework provides both authentication (verifying who is making the request) and authorization (determining what they are allowed to access).
sections.eli5: Each manager gets their own rules about what they can look at and change. If they try to do something they are not allowed to do, the agent refuses.

sections.title: Conformance and Instrumentation
sections.content: SNMPv2 defines conformance statements specifying acceptable lower bounds of implementation and actual implementation levels. Compliance statements describe requirements for agents with respect to object definitions using the MODULE-COMPLIANCE macro. Capability statements describe agent capabilities with respect to object definitions using the AGENT-CAPABILITIES macro. Collections of related objects are grouped together using the OBJECT-GROUP macro to form units of conformance. The Management Information Base for SNMPv2 defines managed objects describing the behavior of SNMPv2 entities, and the Manager-to-Manager MIB defines managed objects for SNMPv2 entities acting in a manager role, with extensions expected to be defined in the future.
sections.eli5: Everyone agrees on what information managers must be able to get and what they should optionally support. This helps vendors build equipment that will work together.
